question: By whom did the burden of the word of the LORD come unto Israel according to the opening superscription of the book?
opt1: Malachi
opt2: Zechariah
opt3: Haggai
opt4: Nehemiah
correct: Malachi
explanation: Malachi 1:1 identifies the prophet and the divine oracle delivered unto Israel: Malachi 1:1 (KJV) - "The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi."

question: When Israel cynically questioned God's love saying, 'Wherein hast thou loved us?', what historical brotherly relationship did the LORD cite to demonstrate His sovereign election?
opt1: His deliverance of Isaac from Mount Moriah rather than Ishmael
opt2: His love for Jacob and hatred of Esau, whose heritage He laid waste
opt3: His election of Judah to bear the sceptre instead of Reuben
opt4: His preservation of Joseph in Egypt above all his brethren
correct: His love for Jacob and hatred of Esau, whose heritage He laid waste
explanation: Malachi 1:2-3 emphasizes God's sovereign covenant choice of Jacob over his twin brother Esau: Malachi 1:2 (KJV) - "I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob,"

question: When Edom boasts that they will return and rebuild their desolate places, what title of perpetual judgment does the LORD of hosts declare they shall be called?
opt1: The valley of slaughter and the habitation of dragons
opt2: The wilderness of salt and the remnant of destruction
opt3: The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever
opt4: The mountain of pride and the inheritance of everlasting sorrow
correct: The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever
explanation: Malachi 1:4 records God's irrevocable sentence against Edom's arrogant rebuilding: Malachi 1:4 (KJV) - "Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the LORD of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the LORD hath indignation for ever."

question: In confronting the priests who despised His name, what foundational familial and social analogy does the LORD employ regarding filial honor and reverence?
opt1: A soldier obeyeth his commander and a subject his king
opt2: A disciple followeth his master and a shepherd his flock
opt3: A craftsman guideth his apprentice and a bride reverenceth her husband
opt4: A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master
correct: A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master
explanation: Malachi 1:6 exposes the priests' utter lack of reverence toward God as their Father and Master: Malachi 1:6 (KJV) - "A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the LORD of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name. And ye say, Wherein have we despised thy name?"

question: How did the priests pollute the sacred altar of the LORD while defensively asking, 'Wherein have we polluted thee?'
opt1: By offering polluted bread and diseased, blind, and lame sacrifices upon the altar
opt2: By burning strange fire and pagan frankincense imported from Moab
opt3: By withholding the morning and evening burnt offerings to feast themselves
opt4: By sprinkling the blood of swine upon the four horns of the altar
correct: By offering polluted bread and diseased, blind, and lame sacrifices upon the altar
explanation: Malachi 1:7-8 condemns the priests for presenting unacceptable, contaminated offerings upon the altar: Malachi 1:7 (KJV) - "Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar; and ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say, The table of the LORD is contemptible."

question: To demonstrate the offensive indignity of offering blind, lame, and sick animals to God, to whom does the LORD challenge the priests to present such gifts?
opt1: Unto the high priest of the temple
opt2: Unto their civil governor
opt3: Unto the king of Persia
opt4: Unto the elders of the city gate
correct: Unto their civil governor
explanation: Malachi 1:8 uses the civil governor to highlight how an earthly ruler would despise gifts that the priests dared offer to God: Malachi 1:8 (KJV) - "And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What solemn lament does the LORD utter concerning the mercenary spirit of the temple ministers who refused even basic service without payment?
opt1: Who among you will minister at the altar without demanding the priest's portion?
opt2: Why tread ye my courts when your hearts are set upon silver and grain?
opt3: Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought
opt4: Is there any Levite who will guard the sanctuary thresholds without wages of deceit?
correct: Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought
explanation: Malachi 1:10 shows God's rejection of mercenary temple rituals performed without heart or love: Malachi 1:10 (KJV) - "Who is there even among you that would shut the doors for nought? neither do ye kindle fire on mine altar for nought. I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand."

question: In contrast to Israel's corrupt sacrifices, how does the LORD describe the pure global worship that will be offered unto His name among the Gentiles?
opt1: From the mountains of Lebanon to the ends of the sea shall bulls be slain on high places
opt2: Every monarch of the earth shall send tribute of gold and cedar to the temple at Jerusalem
opt3: All families of the earth shall keep the Feast of Tabernacles and offer unblemished lambs
opt4: From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering
correct: From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering
explanation: Malachi 1:11 proclaims a magnificent Messianic prophecy of universal Gentile worship: Malachi 1:11 (KJV) - "For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What disdainful complaint did the priests utter regarding divine altar service, demonstrating their utter contempt for holy things?
opt1: Behold, what a weariness is it!
opt2: The altar is clean enough for common beasts!
opt3: Where is the profit in standing before the Lord?
opt4: Why should we sacrifice the finest of the flock?
correct: Behold, what a weariness is it!
explanation: Malachi 1:13 records the weary, contemptuous attitude of the priests toward their sacred calling: Malachi 1:13 (KJV) - "Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD."

question: Why does the LORD pronounce a divine curse upon the deceiver who hath in his flock a male yet voweth and sacrificeth a corrupt thing unto the Lord?
opt1: Because the fire of the altar consumeth only holy flesh
opt2: For I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen
opt3: Because every deceitful vow polluteth the tabernacles of Jacob
opt4: For the blood of a blemished beast bringeth an incurable plague
correct: For I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen
explanation: Malachi 1:14 concludes the chapter with a majestic declaration of God's universal royal majesty: Malachi 1:14 (KJV) - "But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the LORD a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen."

question: What judicial judgment does the LORD threaten against the priests if they will not hear and lay it to heart to give glory unto His name?
opt1: He will smite their firstborn sons and burn their ancestral dwellings
opt2: He will deliver their sacred vestments and tithes to the kings of Babylon
opt3: I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already
opt4: He will silence their lineage and replace them with the sons of Phinehas
correct: I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already
explanation: Malachi 2:2 announces the divine curse falling upon the unrepentant priesthood and their blessings: Malachi 2:2 (KJV) - "If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart."

question: What shocking and humiliating indignity does the LORD declare He will execute upon the corrupt priests concerning their feast offerings?
opt1: He will strip their holy mitres and cast their censers into the brook Kidron
opt2: He will cause their sacred wine to turn to vinegar and their unleavened bread to mold
opt3: He will strike their hands with wasting disease so they cannot lift the blood of bullocks
opt4: Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it
correct: Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it
explanation: Malachi 2:3 depicts the utter dishonor God would bring upon hypocritical priests: Malachi 2:3 (KJV) - "Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it."

question: How does the LORD characterize His original, sacred covenant established with Levi in Malachi 2:5?
opt1: My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name
opt2: My covenant was with him of silver and gold, established for the perpetual service of the tabernacle
opt3: My covenant was with him of sovereignty and dominion over the tribes of Israel
opt4: My covenant was with him of continuous visions and revelations by the Urim and Thummim
correct: My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name
explanation: Malachi 2:5 describes the ideal character of the Levitical covenant founded on life, peace, and holy fear: Malachi 2:5 (KJV) - "My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name."

question: What pristine spiritual attributes distinguished the faithful priest in the true covenant of Levi according to Malachi 2:6?
opt1: He offered daily blood libations and fasted on all solemn assemblies
opt2: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity
opt3: He guarded the sanctuary doors with weapons of brass and pronounced judgments on the kings
opt4: He wore linen garments without spot and preserved the golden candlestick unquenched
correct: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity
explanation: Malachi 2:6 presents the divine portrait of a true spiritual priest: Malachi 2:6 (KJV) - "The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity."

question: According to Malachi 2:7, what is the sacred calling of a priest's lips, and what exalted title is given unto him?
opt1: His lips should speak parabolic mysteries, for he is the seer of the Most High
opt2: His lips should guard the treasury of silver, for he is the steward of the temple
opt3: For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts
opt4: His lips should pronounce victory in battle, for he is the commander of Israel's hosts
correct: For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts
explanation: Malachi 2:7 establishes that the priest is called to be God's teacher and messenger: Malachi 2:7 (KJV) - "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts."

question: Why did the LORD make the contemporary priests contemptible and base before all the people in Malachi 2:9?
opt1: Because they refused to pay tribute to the civil authorities of Persia
opt2: Because they neglected the physical repair of the temple courts
opt3: Because they did not fast on the appointed tenth day of the seventh month
opt4: According as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law
correct: According as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law
explanation: Malachi 2:9 points out their unfaithfulness and partiality in applying God's law: Malachi 2:9 (KJV) - "Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law."

question: What grievous spiritual treachery and abomination did Judah commit in Israel and Jerusalem according to Malachi 2:11?
opt1: Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god
opt2: Judah hath erected altars of Baal within the courts of the house of the Lord
opt3: Judah hath sold the poor for a pair of shoes and trampled the needy
opt4: Judah hath refused circumcision and adopted the dietary abominations of the heathen
correct: Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god
explanation: Malachi 2:11 denounces the covenant unfaithfulness of intermarriage with pagan idolaters: Malachi 2:11 (KJV) - "Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god."

question: Why did the LORD refuse to regard or receive Judah's offerings with good will, despite their covering the altar with weeping and tears?
opt1: Because their wine offerings were diluted and their incense lacked frankincense
opt2: Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant
opt3: Because they failed to bring the full tenth part of the harvest into the storerooms
opt4: Because their hands were stained with innocent blood from unjust civil courts
correct: Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant
explanation: Malachi 2:13-14 identifies treacherous divorce and marital betrayal as the reason God rejected their sacrifices: Malachi 2:14 (KJV) - "Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant."

question: What profound divine purpose did God intend when He made husband and wife one in marriage, and what is His explicit stance on divorce?
opt1: That they might multiply rulers over the earth; and He tolerateth divorce for diverse customs
opt2: That they might build grand houses in Zion; and He overlooketh divorce when sorrow ariseth
opt3: That he might seek a godly seed; and 'the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away'
opt4: That they might increase the Levitical tithes; and He accepteth divorce when an offering is paid
correct: That he might seek a godly seed; and 'the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away'
explanation: Malachi 2:15-16 reveals that God designed marriage to produce godly offspring, stating His hatred of divorce: Malachi 2:16 (KJV) - "For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously."

question: How had the people wearied the LORD with their cynical words, as recorded in Malachi 2:17?
opt1: By complaining that the sabbath was too long and demanding trade on holy days
opt2: By claiming that their ancestors had suffered needlessly during the seventy years of Babylon
opt3: By arguing that sacrifices brought no tangible rain or prosperity to their vineyards
opt4: When ye say, Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them; or, Where is the God of judgment?
correct: When ye say, Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them; or, Where is the God of judgment?
explanation: Malachi 2:17 rebukes moral relativism and doubting God's justice: Malachi 2:17 (KJV) - "Ye have wearied the LORD with your words. Yet ye say, Wherein have we wearied him? When ye say, Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them; or, Where is the God of judgment?"

question: Who does the LORD of hosts declare He will send to prepare the way before Him, and who shall suddenly come to His temple?
opt1: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant
opt2: Behold, I will send Zerubbabel my governor, and Joshua my priest to erect the holy courts
opt3: Behold, I will send Moses the lawgiver, and David the king shall appear in glory upon Mount Zion
opt4: Behold, I will send the archangel Michael, and the heavenly host shall surround the holy place
correct: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the Lord, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant
explanation: Malachi 3:1 prophesies the forerunner (John the Baptist) and the Messiah, the Messenger of the Covenant: Malachi 3:1 (KJV) - "Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the LORD, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: How does Malachi 3:2-3 describe the refining work of the Lord at His coming, particularly toward the sons of Levi?
opt1: He shall be like an unquenchable whirlwind and a sharp threshing instrument
opt2: He is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap: and he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi
opt3: He shall be like a rushing river cleansing the temple courts with living waters
opt4: He shall be like a consuming earthquake casting down all unrighteous altars
correct: He is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap: and he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver: and he shall purify the sons of Levi
explanation: Malachi 3:2-3 depicts the intensive spiritual purification brought by the Messiah: Malachi 3:2 (KJV) - "But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap:"

question: Against which specific groups of moral and social transgressors does the LORD declare He will be a swift witness in judgment in Malachi 3:5?
opt1: Those who break the Sabbath, worship upon high hills, and neglect circumcision
opt2: Scribes who boast in genealogies, traders who sell doves in the temple, and drunkards
opt3: Against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and that turn aside the stranger from his right
opt4: Priests who accept unclean tithes, kings who multiply wives, and warriors who shed blood
correct: Against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and that turn aside the stranger from his right
explanation: Malachi 3:5 lists the social and moral sins that invite God's swift judgment: Malachi 3:5 (KJV) - "And I will come near to you to judgment; and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against false swearers, and against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless, and that turn aside the stranger from his right, and fear not me, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What fundamental theological truth regarding God's unchangeable character guarantees that the sons of Jacob are not utterly consumed?
opt1: Because my compassion is renewed every morning upon Mount Zion
opt2: For I have sworn by my throne that David's line shall endure for ever
opt3: Because the blood of the covenant ever speaketh on the golden mercy seat
opt4: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed
correct: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed
explanation: Malachi 3:6 grounds Israel's preservation in the immutable, unchangeable nature and faithfulness of God: Malachi 3:6 (KJV) - "For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed."

question: When the LORD charges the whole nation with robbing Him, in what specific spiritual stewardship had they committed this robbery?
opt1: In tithes and offerings
opt2: In firstborn sons and sheep
opt3: In frankincense and sacred oil
opt4: In gold vessels and temple timber
correct: In tithes and offerings
explanation: Malachi 3:8 identifies withholding tithes and offerings as robbing God Himself: Malachi 3:8 (KJV) - "Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me. But ye say, Wherein have we robbed thee? In tithes and offerings."

question: What divine challenge and promise does the LORD give concerning the bringing of all tithes into the storehouse in Malachi 3:10?
opt1: Offer forty shekels for each priest, and I will multiply your silver beyond the kings of the east
opt2: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith... if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it
opt3: Lay your harvest at the temple gate, and I will cause grain to sprout upon the barren rocks
opt4: Consecrate your firstfruits on the new moon, and an angel shall guard your olive groves from hail
correct: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith... if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it
explanation: Malachi 3:10 invites the people to test God's overwhelming generosity through faithful tithing: Malachi 3:10 (KJV) - "Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it."

question: What specific agricultural blessing and protection does the LORD promise unto those who honor Him with their tithes?
opt1: He will send early and latter rains in double measure so wheat shall grow in the wilderness
opt2: He will cause the soil to yield three harvests in a single season without tilling
opt3: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field
opt4: He will drive away foreign armies so they shall never tread upon the threshing floors of Judah
correct: And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field
explanation: Malachi 3:11 assures divine protection against crop-destroying pests and premature vine drop: Malachi 3:11 (KJV) - "And I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not destroy the fruits of your ground; neither shall your vine cast her fruit before the time in the field, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What insolent words did the cynical skeptics speak against God regarding the perceived vanity of serving the LORD?
opt1: God hath forgotten the earth and dwelleth only in the distant heavens
opt2: The prophets of Israel have spoken lies and the law of Moses is an intolerable burden
opt3: Why should we sacrifice when our fathers perished in the exile of Babylon?
opt4: Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts? And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up
correct: Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts? And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up
explanation: Malachi 3:14-15 exposes the bitter words of those who claimed piety yielded no earthly reward: Malachi 3:14 (KJV) - "Ye have said, It is vain to serve God: and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance, and that we have walked mournfully before the LORD of hosts?"

question: In the midst of pervasive cynicism, how did the faithful remnant respond, and what heavenly record was established on their behalf?
opt1: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name
opt2: They tore their garments and fasted forty days before the water gate of Jerusalem
opt3: They fled into the hills of Ephraim and formed holy communities dedicated to the law
opt4: They presented twenty bullocks upon the altar and wrote a new covenant upon stone tablets
correct: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name
explanation: Malachi 3:16 records God's tender regard and the book of remembrance written for those who reverenced His name: Malachi 3:16 (KJV) - "Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name."

question: How does the LORD affectionately describe the faithful in Malachi 3:17, and what discernment will be revealed when He acts?
opt1: They shall be crowned as princes; and they shall judge all the heathen nations with an iron sceptre
opt2: And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him. Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked
opt3: They shall be like pillars of brass in the temple; and they shall receive the double portion of Jacob
opt4: They shall inherit all the treasures of the Gentiles; and their names shall be proclaimed in the gates
correct: And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him. Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked
explanation: Malachi 3:17-18 reveals that God considers the faithful His special treasure (jewels) and will make clear the distinction between righteous and wicked: Malachi 3:17 (KJV) - "And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him."

question: How does Malachi 4:1 describe the apocalyptic heat and total destruction of the coming Day of the LORD upon the proud and wicked?
opt1: A flood of brimstone shall sweep down from the mountains and carry them into the sea
opt2: A sudden pestilence shall smite their flesh and their strong men shall fall like autumn leaves
opt3: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch
opt4: A tempest of hail and lightning shall shatter their strongholds until no wall remaineth standing
correct: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch
explanation: Malachi 4:1 pictures the day of judgment as an oven burning the wicked like dry stubble: Malachi 4:1 (KJV) - "For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch."

question: What glorious Messianic promise is given unto those that fear the LORD's name in Malachi 4:2?
opt1: Unto you shall the Star of Jacob shine with eternal wisdom and guide your steps
opt2: Unto you shall the Branch of David bring forth abundance and peace upon all borders
opt3: Unto you shall the river of life flow with gladness and wipe away all your tears
opt4: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall
correct: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall
explanation: Malachi 4:2 contains the famous Messianic title Sun of Righteousness bringing healing and joyful liberation: Malachi 4:2 (KJV) - "But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall."

question: What triumphant vindication is prophesied for the righteous over the wicked in the day of the LORD's consummation?
opt1: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts
opt2: And ye shall bind the wicked in heavy chains of iron and deliver them to outer darkness
opt3: And ye shall watch them flee into the caverns of the rocks before the brightness of His coming
opt4: And ye shall inherit their vineyards, orchards, and palaces in the midst of Jerusalem
correct: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts
explanation: Malachi 4:3 foretells the complete overthrow of the wicked, who become like ashes under the feet of the righteous: Malachi 4:3 (KJV) - "And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do this, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What foundational statutory charge is issued to all Israel as the prophetic voice prepares to fall silent until the New Testament era?
opt1: Keep ye the covenants of David and Solomon regarding the royal throne
opt2: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments
opt3: Observe ye the holy ordinances delivered unto Abraham regarding circumcision and faith
opt4: Meditate day and night upon the proverbs and psalms of the ancient kings
correct: Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments
explanation: Malachi 4:4 directs the people back to the foundational revelation of God given through Moses at Horeb: Malachi 4:4 (KJV) - "Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments."

question: Whom does the LORD promise to send before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD in Malachi 4:5?
opt1: Moses the lawgiver
opt2: Samuel the judge
opt3: Elijah the prophet
opt4: Jeremiah the prophet
correct: Elijah the prophet
explanation: Malachi 4:5 promises the coming of Elijah the prophet before the great Day of the Lord (fulfilled typologically in John the Baptist): Malachi 4:5 (KJV) - "Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD:"

question: What ministry of generational reconciliation and spiritual restoration will Elijah perform when he comes?
opt1: He shall rebuild the twelve fallen altars of Israel upon Mount Carmel
opt2: He shall slay the false prophets with the sword and call down fire from heaven
opt3: He shall crown the governor of Judah and restore the royal house of David
opt4: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers
correct: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers
explanation: Malachi 4:6 outlines the reconciliatory mission of Elijah turning the hearts of parents and children to one another: Malachi 4:6 (KJV) - "And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse."

question: With what warning of divine consequence does the entire Old Testament canon solemnly conclude in the final clause of Malachi 4:6?
opt1: lest I come and smite the earth with a curse
opt2: lest my presence depart from Zion for ever
opt3: lest the Gentiles inherit the holy sanctuary
opt4: lest the name of Jacob be blotted out from the earth
correct: lest I come and smite the earth with a curse
explanation: The closing verse of the Old Testament ends with a sobering warning if reconciliation does not occur: Malachi 4:6 (KJV) - "lest I come and smite the earth with a curse."

question: In Malachi 4, what dramatic thematic contrast is established between the fate of the arrogant wicked and that of the humble God-fearers?
opt1: The wicked are cast into deep pits of water while the righteous walk upon high hills
opt2: The wicked are burned as rootless stubble while the righteous experience healing wings and joy like stall-fed calves
opt3: The wicked are smitten with blindness while the righteous behold visions of the third heaven
opt4: The wicked wander in perpetual exile while the righteous build palaces in Jerusalem
correct: The wicked are burned as rootless stubble while the righteous experience healing wings and joy like stall-fed calves
explanation: Malachi 4:1-2 contrasts the fire of destruction for the proud with the healing warmth of the Sun of Righteousness for the reverent: Malachi 4:1 (KJV) - "For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch."

question: Which two supreme representatives of the Old Covenant—one embodying the Law and the other the Prophets—are explicitly mentioned in the closing verses of Malachi?
opt1: Abraham and Isaiah
opt2: David and Ezekiel
opt3: Moses and Elijah
opt4: Joshua and Daniel
correct: Moses and Elijah
explanation: Malachi 4:4-5 brings together Moses (the Lawgiver at Horeb) and Elijah (the Prophet), who later appeared together with Jesus at the Transfiguration: Malachi 4:4 (KJV) - "Remember ye the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments."

question: What metaphor does Malachi 4:2 use to portray the uncontainable joy, liberation, and vigorous growth of those who receive healing from the Sun of righteousness?
opt1: Ye shall soar as eagles above the mountain heights
opt2: Ye shall leap upon the crags like young harts
opt3: Ye shall flourish like green olive trees by rivers of water
opt4: and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall
correct: and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall
explanation: Malachi 4:2 vividly illustrates the jubilant freedom of the redeemed like young calves released from their stalls: Malachi 4:2 (KJV) - "and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall."
